title: KV cache: profile-based compaction thresholds + fragmentation/compaction metrics
author: Omar El-Sayed
release_notes: Add compaction + fragmentation counters for KV cache, tagged by profile_id/sku.
Move KV compaction trigger thresholds into hardware profile pack with safe defaults for H100/L40S.
body:
Context
We’ve seen two recurring issues during profile-pack bring-up:
(1) L40S stability: intermittent OOM under burst traffic correlated with allocator fragmentation and late compaction (SUP-21958).
(2) H100 tail latency spikes when compaction triggers too aggressively under mixed workloads.

This PR makes compaction behavior explicitly configurable per hardware profile, and adds the minimum viable metrics to validate expected behavior and support on-call triage.

What’s in this PR
- Profile-based compaction thresholds
  - Adds per-profile knobs for when to trigger KV cache compaction and how much headroom to preserve.
  - Moves existing hard-coded thresholds behind profile defaults (no behavior change unless profile pack is enabled).
  - Adds validation/guardrails to prevent unsafe configs (e.g., compaction disabled with low headroom, or thresholds that would guarantee pathological churn).
- New metrics/counters (exported via runtime metrics)
  - kv_cache_compaction_runs_total{profile_id,sku,reason}
  - kv_cache_compaction_time_ms{profile_id,sku} (histogram)
  - kv_cache_compaction_bytes_moved_total{profile_id,sku}
  - kv_cache_fragmentation_estimate{profile_id,sku} (gauge)
  - kv_cache_free_bytes{profile_id,sku} and kv_cache_reserved_bytes{profile_id,sku} (gauges)
  - kv_cache_oom_prevented_total{profile_id,sku} (counter; increments when admission control would have OOM’ed without compaction + headroom enforcement)
- Logging / debug
  - On compaction run, emit a single structured log line with: profile_id, sku, reason, time_ms, bytes_moved, frag_before, frag_after.
  - Adds these to the existing “runtime startup summary” log when profile pack is enabled so we can correlate behavior with config.

Defaults (profile pack)
- H100 (sxm + pcie):
  - Higher tolerance for fragmentation; compaction triggers later to avoid churn.
  - Target: keep p99 stable on mixed prompt length workloads.
- L40S:
  - Earlier compaction + stricter headroom preservation to reduce OOM risk during bursts.
  - Target: keep OOM rate near-zero at the cost of a small throughput hit under very high concurrency.

Behavioral expectations / trade-offs
- Earlier compaction will increase background memory movement; expect small increases in compaction_time_ms and potentially mild p95 impact if compaction overlaps with decode-heavy periods.
- Later compaction reduces churn but can increase fragmentation_estimate and raises OOM risk under bursty allocation patterns; this is why L40S defaults skew “safer”.

Bench results (benchmark-lab quick pass)
- H100: No statistically significant p50 change; p99 improved ~2–4% in the mixed workload bucket due to fewer compaction-triggered stalls.
- L40S: OOMs eliminated in the bursty concurrency bucket at the recommended cap; throughput down ~1–2% due to more frequent compaction. (Numbers are in the linked ENG-4926 run notes.)

Rollout notes
- Metrics are tagged with profile_id and sku; cardinality is bounded by the profile pack (expected < 20 active values).
- This is compatible with the Hosted canary plan and should improve incident visibility; the L40S defaults specifically address the failure mode in SUP-21958.

Commits
1) runtime/kv: introduce CompactionPolicy struct and reasons enum
2) runtime/profiles: add kv_cache.compaction_thresholds to profile schema + defaults
3) runtime/metrics: export compaction histograms and fragmentation estimate gauges
4) runtime/logging: structured compaction log + startup summary fields
5) tests: add unit tests for guardrails and “compaction triggers by threshold”

Files / areas changed (high level)
- runtime/kv_cache/*
- runtime/profiles/schema/*
- runtime/observability/metrics/*
- runtime/config/*
- runtime/tests/*

Reviewer notes
- Please sanity-check the guardrails: the goal is to make it hard to configure ourselves into compaction thrash or guaranteed OOM.
- Naming: I went with “fragmentation_estimate” because we do not have a precise allocator view; open to better naming but I’d like the metric to clearly be approximate.

Follow-ups (out of scope)
- Wire compaction_time_ms and fragmentation_estimate into the Runtime Profiles dashboard panels (tracked in ENG-4931).
- Consider per-model-family overrides if we see systematic differences between MoE vs dense models under long context windows.

Links
- Linear: ENG-4926 (KV cache + fragmentation guardrails)
- Jira: SUP-21958 (L40S intermittent OOM under burst traffic)

Review conversation
Samir Qureshi (requested changes): The L40S defaults look safer, but I want explicit validation that compaction won’t run back-to-back in a tight loop. Can we add a minimum interval or dampening?
Omar El-Sayed (author): Good catch. Added a dampening window (min_compaction_interval_ms) and a “bytes_moved < threshold” early-exit to avoid churn. Also added a unit test that simulates repeated triggers.

Noah Patel (comment): Are we confident fragmentation_estimate won’t cause confusion? We should document how it’s computed.
Omar El-Sayed: Added inline docs + a short note in the metrics README: it’s computed from (reserved_bytes - largest_free_block_estimate)/reserved_bytes, where largest_free_block_estimate is derived from allocator telemetry when available, otherwise from our KV segment free list heuristic.

Allison Grant (comment): Please ensure the histograms use the standard latency buckets and are tagged with profile_id/sku only (no model label).
Omar El-Sayed: Updated to reuse the standard duration buckets and removed the temporary model tag.

Julian Moore (approval): Looks good; structured log line will help with trace correlation. Approved.

CI
- buildkite/redwood: build ✅
- buildkite/redwood: unit tests ✅
- buildkite/redwood: perf-smoke (H100) ✅
- lint/format ✅

Merge
- Merged via squash on 2026-02-10.
- Notes: Safe behind profile pack enablement; defaults only take effect when profile pack is active.
